stash:datasets.title: Data and code for: Peatland carbon responses to elevated CO₂ and warming in the SPRUCE experiment
stash:datasets.abstract: This repository contains processed and derived data, model code, and analysis scripts associated with the study “Elevated CO₂ mitigated warming-enhanced carbon loss from northern peatland.” The dataset is based on the Spruce and Peatland Responses Under Changing Environments (SPRUCE) experiment, which applies five levels of whole-ecosystem warming under ambient and elevated atmospheric CO₂ conditions in a northern peatland. The dataset includes processed observational and model-derived variables used to quantify ecosystem carbon dynamics, gross primary productivity (GPP), carbon uptake phenology, and their responses to warming and elevated CO₂. The repository also contains the TECO-SPRUCE model code and Python scripts used for data processing, statistical analyses, and figure generation. These materials can be reused to reproduce the analyses presented in the associated article and to investigate peatland carbon-cycle responses to warming and elevated CO₂. The dataset contains no personally identifiable or sensitive information.

stash:datasets.title: Data from:  The Duntulm sauropod tracksite and environmental partitioning in Middle Jurassic dinosaurs on the Isle of Skye, Scotland
stash:datasets.abstract: Dinosaur fossils from the Isle of Skye (Scotland, UK), particularly the abundant trace fossil record, provide a window into dinosaur evolution during the poorly known Middle Jurassic. Here we present the photogrammetric models, orthophotos, and underlying photosets and ground control points underpinning a comprehensive description of the Duntulm tracksite from Cairidh Ghlumaig Bay. We used this data to create whole site maps, catalogue the tracks, and identify trackways. The tracksite is dominated by small to medium-sized (<75 cm) sauropod footprints spanning several preservation styles, from casts with details of toes to impressions with less distinct features. Several short, narrow-gauge trackways indicate the sauropods were moving with a walking gait, and the wide range of orientations of the trackways does not indicate any gregarious behavior. Sparse, isolated theropod footprints are also present along the Duntulm coastline. We then examined the relationship between Skye's dinosaur trackmakers and the substrate in which the footprints are found. We found that Skye's sauropods had a preference for lagoonal substrates, while 'non-sauropod' dinosaurs (theropods, thyreophorans, and ornithopods) are more abundant in subaerially exposed mudflats.

stash:datasets.methods: We used two unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) with payloads of cameras oriented at nadir to survey the main track-bearing platform at Duntulm. In total, we flew six flights at 6 m above the ground surface. We used the resulting 554 images to construct photogrammetric models of the Duntulm tracksite in Agisoft Metashape Version 1.8.4. This model was constrained with ground control points (GCPs) from relative carrier-phase GNSS (Global Navigation Satellite System) data collection with the reference station (Lochcarron – LCAR; ~60 km distance). The photogrammetric model and subsequent orthophotos were used for dinosaur footprint descriptions and measurements of trackway characteristics.

stash:datasets.title: Data and code from: Rapid evolution of body size in response to consistent natural selection in a wild lizard
stash:datasets.abstract: Although directional selection and additive genetic variance are frequently detected in wild populations, evolutionary responses are often weak or absent, giving rise to a “paradox of stasis.” To explore the relationship between selection and evolution, we used a pedigreed wild population of lizards (Anolis sagrei) to quantify natural selection, estimate additive genetic (co)variances, and track phenotypic and genetic change in adult body size while addressing several factors that could lead to evolutionary stasis. Selection via adult reproductive success consistently favored larger body size in both sexes and was stronger in males. Body size was heritable and genetically correlated with adult reproductive success in both sexes, indicating that selection acted on underlying additive genetic variance. Across five annual cohorts, mean phenotypic values and breeding values for body size increased in both sexes, exceeding expectations under genetic drift. This rapid evolutionary response was not obscured by several processes commonly invoked to explain stasis. For example, accounting for phenotypic skew strengthened expected responses, and prior viability selection on juveniles did not phenotypically or genetically oppose selection on adult body size. Our results show that rapid evolutionary change is detectable in the wild when directional selection is consistent, acts on additive genetic variance, and is not genetically opposed by early-life viability selection.

stash:datasets.title: Electrocardiographic screening for left atrial enlargement in dogs: Derivation and validation of an algorithm combining lead II P-wave duration and the Morris index
stash:datasets.abstract: Combining electrocardiographic measurements may improve identification of dogs requiring echocardiographic assessment. This retrospective diagnostic accuracy study derived a three-category algorithm in 150 dogs and evaluated it in 50 separate validation dogs. Three observers independently measured lead II P-wave duration and the V1 Morris index, with observer A providing the primary analysis. Left atrium-to-aorta ratio (LA/Ao) ≥1.6 was the primary outcome; normalized left ventricular internal diameter in diastole (LVIDDN) ≥1.7 was evaluated independently as a secondary outcome. Thresholds from 114 reference dogs were 48 and 52 ms for P duration and 3.04 mV·ms for Morris. Positive triage comprised intermediate and high categories. Primary-outcome sensitivity and specificity were 90.6% and 50.0% in derivation and 100% and 85.7% in validation. Validation sensitivity had a 95% confidence interval of 88.1%–100%. The ordinal algorithm area under the curve was 0.961 in validation, compared with 0.868 for P and 0.844 for Morris; paired differences were not significant after Holm adjustment. Secondary-outcome validation sensitivity and specificity were 88.0% and 60.0%. The algorithm provided complementary detection of left atrial enlargement and reproducible measurements across observers, supporting further evaluation as an adjunct to echocardiographic triage.
stash:datasets.methods:
Study population

Reporting was guided by STARD 2015 and STROBE-Vet recommendations (Bossuyt et al. 2015; Cohen et al. 2016; O’Connor et al. 2016). This retrospective diagnostic accuracy study included 150 dogs in a derivation cohort and 50 dogs in a separate validation cohort. Derivation examinations were performed at the veterinary diagnostic imaging center NUDIVE, Federal University of Piauí (UFPI), Brazil, between July 2024 and June 2025. Eligibility required a 12-lead electrocardiogram (ECG) and complete echocardiographic examination obtained on the same day. All 200 dogs were included in the principal analyses. The sample comprised the available eligible records; no prospective sample-size calculation was documented. American College of Veterinary Internal Medicine (ACVIM) stages were recorded using the consensus framework (Keene et al. 2019). The study was approved by the UFPI Animal Use Ethics Committee (CEUA/UFPI; protocol 824/2024), and written owner consent was obtained.

Electrocardiographic acquisition and measurements

ECGs were recorded with a digital 12-lead INCardio X system with dogs in right lateral recumbency without sedation, at 50 mm/s and 10 mm/mV, for 3 min. V1 placement followed the precordial lead system described by Santilli et al. (2019). Three observers, designated A, B, and C, independently measured the ECGs while blinded to the other readings and clinical and echocardiographic findings. When baseline instability, artifacts, or indistinct wave boundaries prevented reliable measurement, other readable regions of the same tracing were examined under the same blinding conditions.

Each stored ECG value represented the automatically generated mean of three measurements. Individual measurements were not retained; therefore, within-tracing repeatability could not be assessed. P-wave duration in lead II was expressed in milliseconds. The Morris index was calculated as the duration of the terminal negative P-wave component in V1 multiplied by its absolute amplitude, in mV·ms. Measurement of the terminal negative component and calculation of the index are illustrated in Fig. 1. P-wave termination was referenced to the isoelectric T–P baseline when the P–R segment was sloped. In derivation, the PR interval was calculated as lead II P duration plus the PR segment, and the Macruz index as P duration divided by the PR segment. PR and Macruz were ancillary variables and did not enter the algorithm.

Echocardiographic reference

One echocardiographer, blinded to ECG results, performed the reference examinations using a GE Vivid iq v203 system. LA/Ao was measured in early diastole in the right parasternal short-axis view at the aortic valve level, following the ACVIM approach (Keene et al. 2019). LA/Ao ≥1.6 defined the primary outcome of left atrial enlargement. Left ventricular internal diameter in diastole (LVIDd), LVIDDN, and peak early diastolic transmitral E velocity were measured by the same echocardiographer. LVIDDN was calculated as LVIDd in centimeters divided by body weight in kilograms raised to 0.294 (Cornell et al. 2004). LVIDDN ≥1.7 defined the secondary outcome, independently of LA/Ao. A single reference examination was shared by all ECG observers for each dog.

Data management and algorithm derivation

Records were matched by animal identifier. Checks included completeness, duplicate identifiers, agreement of shared echocardiographic measurements, consistency of derived variables, and the relationship between terminal V1 duration and total P duration in lead II. Each dog contributed one stored value per variable and observer. No principal measurement was imputed. Observer A provided the primary diagnostic analysis; B and C were evaluated separately without averaging ECG readings across observers.

The reference subgroup comprised derivation dogs in ACVIM stages A or B1 with LA/Ao <1.6. Empirical type 7 quantiles from observer A defined the 70th and 90th percentiles of P duration and the 70th percentile of Morris. The resulting decision rule assigned score 2 when P ≥52 ms or when P ≥48 ms and Morris ≥3.04 mV·ms; score 0 required P <48 ms and Morris <3.04 mV·ms; all other combinations received score 1 (Fig. 2). Categories were termed low, intermediate and high and represented increasing electrical evidence of enlargement, rather than predicted future events. Scores 1–2 defined positive triage, equivalent to P ≥48 ms or Morris ≥3.04 mV·ms. Score 2 alone was assessed as a more selective operating point. All thresholds were fixed for validation, other observers and the secondary outcome.

Statistical analysis

Continuous characteristics were summarized using medians and interquartile ranges; counts and percentages described categorical variables. Diagnostic performance included sensitivity, specificity, positive and negative predictive values, accuracy and likelihood ratios. Proportions received exact Clopper–Pearson 95% confidence intervals (CIs) (Clopper and Pearson 1934); likelihood-ratio intervals used the log approximation when estimable. Receiver operating characteristic analysis used the ordinal score and continuous P and Morris values. Areas under the curve (AUCs), CIs, and within-cohort paired comparisons were calculated using DeLong covariance estimates (DeLong et al. 1988). Between-cohort results were described separately.

Paired proportions were compared within McNemar’s framework (McNemar 1947), using two-sided exact conditional tests for sensitivity among outcome-positive dogs, specificity among outcome-negative dogs, and accuracy among all dogs. This implementation controls the nominal type I error rate but can be conservative and have reduced power (Fagerland et al. 2013). Holm adjustment was applied to the three marker pairs within each cohort, observer, outcome, and metric (Aickin and Gensler 1996). Associations between categories and outcomes were assessed with the Fisher–Freeman–Halton exact test; pairwise category comparisons used Fisher exact tests with Holm adjustment. B and C underwent the same analyses against the shared reference. Paired observer comparisons used corresponding three-comparison families. All tests were two-sided; adjusted p <0.05 indicated statistical evidence within the specified family.

Between-observer agreement of stored P and Morris means was assessed using the two-way absolute-agreement intraclass correlation coefficient for a single observer value, ICC(A,1) (McGraw and Wong 1996; Koo and Li 2016). Confidence intervals were estimated using 3,000 dog-level bootstrap samples, with complete observer sets retained during resampling (Efron 1979). Bland–Altman bias and limits of agreement were calculated for each observer pair (Bland and Altman 1986). Linear-weighted kappa assessed ordinal scores (Cohen 1968), and unweighted kappa assessed triage decisions (Cohen 1960). Friedman and paired Wilcoxon tests examined observer differences (Friedman 1937; Wilcoxon 1945).

An exploratory stratified five-fold derivation check re-estimated thresholds within each training reference subgroup and applied them to held-out dogs. This internal check evaluated the development procedure within the available derivation sample, consistent with the distinction between apparent performance and performance assessed by resampling (Steyerberg et al. 2001). Additional analyses included ancillary PR/Macruz discrimination, descriptive Spearman correlations, and exploratory net benefit of fixed referral strategies (Vickers and Elkin 2006; Vickers et al. 2019). Supplementary methods, tables and figures provide complete specifications and results.[1]

Analyses were performed in Python 3.12.14 with NumPy 2.3.5, pandas 2.2.3, SciPy 1.17.0, and scikit-learn 1.8.0; figures were produced with Matplotlib 3.10.8. Code, exact package versions, and the random seed (20260910) are provided with the data.

[1] Supplementary methods, Tables S1–S8, Figures S1–S4 and the data and code archive accompany this article.

stash:datasets.title: Data and code from: Dispersal-limited birds at high risk from cattle farming deforestation in tropical forests
stash:datasets.abstract: We explore the question: how do farming activities affect functional diversity and species traits across different spatial scales in tropical forests? This dataset uses outputs from multispecies occupancy models from Socolar and Mills et al. (2025) to estimate avian communities across 13 different biogeographic units at near-national scales in Colombia. We quantify changes in functional diversity resulting from forest-to-pasture conversion and identify the most impacted functional dimension. Includes computing occupancy community-weighted means, regression modelling of occupancy change across functional dimensions, and cumulative changes in functional metrics at increasing scales. Results indicate that functional diversity metrics are only slightly affected across ecoregions and largely reflect the national scale of loss, driven by a moderate reduction in Functional Richness across scales. particularly affects birds with functional traits related to low dispersal capability.

stash:datasets.title: Blow fly sampling in Southern California, 2022-2023

affiliations.organization: John Jay College of Criminal Justice

stash:datasets.abstract: This dataset includes blow fly (Diptera: Calliphoridae) communities across four ecoregions in Southern California, and local environmental conditions measured using data loggers or nearby weather stations. Collected between 2022 and 2023, the dataset includes collection date, seasonal classification, environmental variables (temperature and relative humidity), trap duration, geographic location (latitude, longitude, ecoregion), and detailed species data (sex-specific and total counts). Environmental data were sourced from HOBO loggers or weather stations and aligned with sampling events. These data support investigations of metacommunity structure, particularly the roles of environmental filtering and dispersal across spatial scales. The dataset enables reuse in studies of necrophagous insect ecology, climate change impacts, and biodiversity monitoring in fragmented landscapes. No personally identifiable or ethically sensitive information is included. Users should cite the dataset when used and consult associated publications for methodological context and analytical frameworks.

stash:datasets.title: A multi-omic atlas reveals distinct immune landscapes in preterm and term chronic placental inflammation
stash:datasets.abstract: Chronic placental inflammation (CPI) comprises a spectrum of chronic inflammatory lesions associated with preterm birth (PTB), yet its cellular and molecular determinants across gestation remain poorly defined. Here, we constructed an integrated multi-omic atlas of CPI by profiling placental and extraplacental tissues from preterm and term pregnancies using imaging mass cytometry, single-cell RNA sequencing, spatial transcriptomics, TCR repertoire mining, and DNA methylation analysis. CPI emerged as a gestational age-dependent immune continuum rather than a uniform inflammatory state. Preterm CPI exhibited unrestricted infiltration of cytotoxic CD8⁺ T cells, activated macrophages, and NK cells forming self-amplifying inflammatory circuits in the extraplacental membranes. In contrast, term CPI exhibited spatially confined immune niches enriched for homeostatic myeloid cells and regulatory T cells, preserving maternal–fetal tolerance despite persistent inflammation. Multi-omic integration revealed active contributions from the developing fetal immune system in preterm CPI, including macrophages, T cells, and mast cells of fetal origin that reshaped maternal–fetal immune communication. Cell–cell communication analyses uncovered pro-inflammatory signaling programs in preterm CPI and resolution-phase pathways in term CPI, while TCR repertoire profiling identified memory clonotypes with viral epitope similarity, consistent with antigen-agnostic activation. Genome-wide DNA methylation analysis revealed CPI-associated epigenetic remodeling linked to developmental and neurocognitive pathways in PTB. Together, this atlas defines the cellular, spatial, and transcriptional architecture of CPI and explains how chronic inflammation drives prematurity and offspring injury, or alternatively remains compatible with term delivery, providing a framework for translational biomarker discovery and therapeutic intervention development.

stash:datasets.title: Data from: Improved use of deep soil water promotes radial growth during drought
stash:datasets.abstract: Increasingly frequent seasonal droughts under rapid climate change threaten the growth stability of subtropical mixed forests across the mid-subtropical monsoon region. In this study, we combined stable hydrogen and oxygen isotope analyses with high–precision radial growth monitoring to explore how water source use influences the radial growth of four subtropical tree species. Three contrasting functional strategies were identified based on rooting depth and water uptake plasticity. First, the shallow water-dependent species (Cupressus funebris Endl.) featured a root system concentrated in the upper soil layer and obtained 38.3% of its water from shallow layers. During the drought period, declining surface soil water availability was accompanied by low stomatal conductance and photosynthetic rates, and the species experienced net stem shrinkage of 1.1 mm. Second, the deep-rooted species (Michelia maudiae Dunn and Abies fabri Craib) exhibited a dual rooting strategy: deep taproots accessed stable water in the 80-100 cm soil layer, which contributed 67.2-75.8% of water uptake during drought, while shallow fine roots captured sporadic rainfall in the upper soil layers. During the drought period, these species maintained relatively high water potentials and positive cumulative radial growth, with annual radial growth 1.9-2.5 times that of C. funebris. Third, the balanced-strategy species (Liquidambar formosana Hance) displayed a relatively uniform root distribution throughout the soil profile, enabling flexible water acquisition across soil layers and sustaining the highest cumulative radial growth during the drought period. Structural equation models revealed that access to stable water sources, particularly deeper reserves as surface soils dried, sustained radial growth indirectly by maintaining stomatal conductance and photosynthesis. This pathway provides a mechanistic explanation for contrasting drought adaptation among subtropical tree species.

stash:datasets.title: Data from: Divergent mandibular morphology in American mink (Neogale vison) fossils suggests novel role in past environments
stash:datasets.abstract: Understanding the presence and spatial distribution of intraspecific morphological variation may shed light on the natural history and ecological breadth, realized and potential, of specific taxa. Insights from the paleontological record can provide additional information on potential phenotypic variation for species that have adapted to past and present environments. Here, we use the American mink (Neogale vison) as a case study to understand the extent and pattern of mandibular shape variation among extant populations (n = 290) and fossil assemblages (n = 13). We placed geometric morphometric landmarks and semilandmarks on 3D models generated from laser light scans of mandibles. A subset of specimens were landmarked in triplicate to assess error. We found that some fossil N. vison mandibles lie outside the morphospace occupied by extant N. vison and are distinct from modern mink. Fossils from Conard Fissure, Arkansas (n = 8) represent a unique morphotype that likely had higher bite forces than modern N. vison. This morphotype may have allowed N. vison at this site to take advantage of larger or different prey. These results demonstrate both the adaptive potential of N. vison and the fossil record’s ability to reveal unique variation in a lineage.

stash:datasets.title: Data from: Population-specific gene expression patterns underlying differential sensitivity to deltamethrin in Culex pipiens in Blida Province, Northern Algeria
stash:datasets.abstract: Insecticide resistance in mosquitoes poses a major challenge for vector control and the prevention of mosquito-borne diseases. This study investigated resistance to the pyrethroid deltamethrin and associated gene expression responses in Culex pipiens populations from Blida Province, Northern Algeria. Larvae were collected from two urban sites (Mouzaia and 13-May) and one rural site (Hammam Melouane), and susceptibility bioassays were conducted using fourth-instar larvae following WHO guidelines. Marked differences in susceptibility were observed among populations. The rural population was highly susceptible (LC₅₀ = 0.00002 ppm), whereas urban populations exhibited strong resistance, with resistance ratios reaching up to 1000-fold. To explore underlying molecular responses, larvae were exposed to LC₂₅, LC₅₀, and LC₇₅ concentrations of deltamethrin, and expression of detoxification, mitochondrial, and digestive enzyme genes was quantified by RT-qPCR. CYP6F1 expression was strongly associated with resistance in the highly resistant urban population, suggesting an important role in metabolic detoxification. In contrast, the susceptible rural population showed pronounced inducible expression of CYP6F1, mitochondrial genes (cytochrome b and COXI), chymotrypsin, and acetylcholinesterase following insecticide exposure, indicating a generalized stress response. These findings reveal population-specific physiological responses to deltamethrin and highlight the complex interplay between detoxification pathways, mitochondrial activity, and protease functions in shaping insecticide responses. The high resistance levels detected in urban populations underscore the need for continuous resistance monitoring and improved vector management strategies.

stash:datasets.title: Data from: A chemical landscape of fear shapes genotype-specific diel vertical migration in Daphnia
stash:datasets.abstract: Understanding how prey perceive and respond to predation risk remains a central challenge in ecology. In aquatic systems, this risk is often communicated through chemical cues released by predators, but it has never been measured directly. In lakes, fish are major predators of the microcrustacean Daphnia, and the fish-derived bile salt 5α-cyprinol sulfate (CPS) has been shown to induce diel vertical migration (DVM) as predator-avoidance behavior in Daphnia. By mapping CPS concentrations across depth and time in a lake and simultaneously quantifying the vertical distribution of Daphnia, we reveal pronounced seasonal and diel variation in perceived predation risk and show that shifts in vertical position correspond to changes in CPS concentrations. Laboratory experiments further show that Daphnia genotypes from the same lake differ strongly in the CPS levels required to trigger DVM, and these thresholds match CPS concentrations observed in the lake. Together, these findings show that environmental variation in a chemically identified predator cue is associated with diel changes in prey distribution and can generate genotype-specific behavioral responses. Our results establish a chemical approach to quantifying the landscape of fear and show how predator-derived chemical signals shape prey movement and ecosystem dynamics.
stash:datasets.methods:
1. Field Sampling:
    • Conducted in Lake Klostersee, Bavaria, Germany, from April to October 2022 to capture seasonal variations.
    • Water samples were collected monthly from six different depth layers (0-2 m, 2-4 m, 4-6 m, 6-8 m, 8-10 m, 10-12 m) using a tube sampler.
    • Additional diel sampling (day and night) was performed on three consecutive days (August 17-19, 2022) at the same depths.
  2. Laboratory Bioassays:
    • Daphnia longispina clones were tested for their response to varying concentrations of 5α-cyprinol sulfate (CPS) using a plankton organ experiment to assess diel vertical migration (DVM).
  3. Chemical Analysis:
  • Solid-phase extraction (SPE): Water samples were processed using C18-SPE cartridges to extract CPS, followed by drying and re-dissolution in methanol.
  • Samples were analyzed using a Vanquish Horizon UHPLC system coupled with a Q-Exactive HF mass spectrometer.
  • Calibration curves for cholesteryl sulfate was used for CPS quantification.

stash:datasets.abstract: During a field expedition to the Jalapão region (Tocantins State, Brazil), a morphologically distinct specimen was collected and identified as a new species, Chamaecrista marinasilvae. Further herbarium investigations revealed additional collections of this taxon from the same state that had been misidentified as Chamaecrista juruenensis. The new species is similar to C. juruenensis in habit, leaflet shape, texture, and coloration, as well as in the general appearance of the inflorescence, but differs in branch color and indumentum, petiolule and pulvinus size, leaflet venation and orientation, and ovary and fruit indumentum. This paper provides a detailed description of the new species, including notes on its morphology, distribution, phenology, taxonomic affinities, and conservation status. A key to the species of Chamaecrista sect. Absus subsect. Absus ser. Absoideae occurring in Tocantins State is also provided.

stash:datasets.title: Data and code from: Wildfire exposure and hazard in the wildland-urban interface
stash:datasets.abstract:
In the decades since the wildland-urban interface (WUI) was first introduced as a priority area in wildfire management, a number of methods for mapping this zone have been developed that each rely on different approaches for identifying the spatial relationship between human habitation and wildland vegetation. Concurrently, simulation-based approaches to identifying values at risk have emerged to estimate wildfire hazard - that is, the likelihood and expected intensity of wildfire - based on fuels, topography, weather, and historical wildfire occurrence.

The aim of this study is to investigate differences between WUI mapping methods, including a novel approach based on historical property records. The WUI mapping method developed herein is based on structure densities from a dataset of historical settlement within the conterminous United States (HISDAC-US). This approach allows for the construction of a longitudinal set of WUI maps from 2000 through 2020 at five-year timesteps, enabling the assessment of regional growth patterns.

I tabulate the spatial extent, population, and number of structures identified as WUI by four different mapping methods within a range of simulated wildfire hazard levels, across a 10x10 km grid that spans the conterminous United States (CONUS). This allows for the comparison of not only values at risk within areas identified as WUI, but also the level of wildfire hazard faced by these values.

stash:datasets.title: Data from: Lessons from a prioritisation process to identify evidence needs at the Woodland Trust, UK
stash:datasets.abstract:
Despite growing acknowledgement and advocacy for the importance of evidence-based conservation, there remain several challenges for conservation organisations to achieve this in reality. Misaligned incentives between academic research and conservation practice can limit the relevance, applicability and accessibility of research. A further challenge is the low number of practitioner-led research agendas that are published with which academics can engage and enable academic-practitioner co-designed research.

To address this challenge, 149 employees from the Woodland Trust were consulted in a series of facilitated workshops and surveys to produce a practitioner-led research agenda. First, an online survey and consultation meetings took place to gather research and evidence questions. Second, subject matter experts collated and synthesised these questions. Third, workshops were run to refine and score research questions using the criteria of overall priority, urgency, and an identifiable pathway to apply research output in conservation practice.

The results of this process are presented in this dataset which includes 173 applied conservation research questions across 14 topic areas and their relative prioritisation score. 

We encourage academics and other researchers working in the sector to review this research agenda and contact the Woodland Trust research team to discuss co-designing future research projects or share current available evidence that addresses research questions within the agenda.

For further information please contact: research@woodlandtrust.org.uk

stash:datasets.abstract: To investigate the linkages between flow reduction (defined as the difference between 21st century and 20th century flows), metabolism, and benthic algae, we measured metabolism and chlorophyll-a concentrations as a proxy of benthic algal biomass in seven desert rivers with varying degrees of flow reduction during July-November in 2023 and 2024. stash:datasets.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a complex autoimmune disease with a substantial heritable component. We performed multi-ancestry genome-wide association meta-analyses of 351,498 individuals (comprising 39,600 RA cases and 311,898 controls) by integrating published and new datasets. This analysis identified 29 novel RA susceptibility loci and systematically classified association signals as population-specific, population-dominant, or population-shared between East Asian and European populations. Bayesian fine-mapping and functional annotation prioritized putative causal variants, highlighting 67 variants with posterior inclusion probability > 0.1 in novel loci, including an SLC27A6 missense variant (rs137898880) and a STIM1 3′ UTR variant (rs3750996). Our gene-prioritization framework combining genetic and biological evidence identified 203 high-confidence effector genes, 16 of which reside in novel loci (e.g., IFI16, AIM2, RGS1, ITPKB, CD80, RHOH, NFKB1, SIK3, and CCND2). Colocalization analysis leveraging tissue-specific eQTL datasets provided mechanistic insights by implicating shared causal variants underlying RA association signals. Notably, the transcription factor gene RUNX3 at a novel locus showed evidence of cis-regulation in immune cells, and RUNX3-binding sites were enriched for variants explaining excess RA heritability, supporting a role for RUNX3 as a trans-regulatory mediator of RA risk at distal RA loci. Finally, gene-drug interaction networks weighted by RA association strength highlighted population-informed therapeutic opportunities and drug-repurposing targets driven largely by novel loci.

stash:datasets.abstract: Interannual variability in both local environmental conditions and basin-scale oceanographic modes of variability is thought to drive larval fish abundance by affecting the timing and location of spawning. We used an extensive compiled dataset of larval fish density from 1995-2018 from continental shelf regions off central California to the Gulf of Alaska to model how sablefish (Anoplopoma fimbria) shifted larval seasonality and geography in response to environmental variability and oceanographic regime shifts. The most predictive spatiotemporal model was the simplest and did not include seasonal or geographic variability, with bottom depth and sea surface temperature as the most predictive environmental covariates. Sablefish larval distributions were centered in the shelf region of the eastern Gulf of Alaska and exhibited correlated shifts among latitudinal, longitudinal, and onshore-offshore center of gravities, but not with seasonal changes. There were few links between geographic and seasonal center of gravities and average environmental conditions, though modeled larval abundance peaked earlier in the year during warmer, spicier average ocean conditions and positive Pacific Decadal Oscillation values. Phase-specific conditional effects models for the Pacific Decadal Oscillation and Oceanic Niño Index showed that sablefish larvae were uniformly associated with water temperatures between 7-8°C while having a more variable relationship with bottom depth. Our results indicate that sablefish larvae demonstrate seasonal shifts in order to maintain a consistent thermal habitat.

stash:datasets.methods:
Sablefish larval data

We collated data from five long-term ichthyoplankton sampling programs covering the region between the Southern California Bight (35° latitude) to the Alaska Peninsula in the western Gulf of Alaska. From north to south, these surveys were the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) Ecosystems and Fisheries Oceanography Coordinated Investigations (EcoFOCI), multiple compiled surveys organized by Department of Fisheries & Oceans Canada (DFO), the NOAA Pre-recruit Survey, Newport Hydrographic Line (NH-Line), and the California Cooperative Oceanic Fisheries Investigations (CalCOFI). Larval data includes samples taken by oblique and paired bongo tows with 236-505 µm mesh from throughout the study area, along with neuston tows from Alaska and southern California. Neuston tows had 505 µm mesh and net openings between 0.13-15 m2. Tows were subset to 1995 to 2018 within the 200 nmi Exclusive Economic Zone within ocean or estuarine waters (salinity ≥ 30 ppt). The northern geographic extent of the area examined was bounded by the latitudinal range of positive tows (59.8°N). We restricted the southern limit to be ≥ 35°N latitude. From north to south, these surveys were the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) Ecosystems and Fisheries Oceanography Coordinated Investigations (EcoFOCI), multiple compiled surveys organized by Department of Fisheries & Oceans Canada (DFO), the NOAA Pre-recruit Survey, Newport Hydrographic Line (NH-Line), and the California Cooperative Oceanic Fisheries Investigations (CalCOFI).

The full datasets of the surveys compiled are available through the following locations/contacts:

- EcoFOCI: By request: https://apps-afsc.fisheries.noaa.gov/ichthyo/index.php 

- Department of Fisheries & Oceans Canada: By request (current contacts are R. Ian Perry or Moira Galbraith)

- NH-Line: By request: https://www.integratedecosystemassessment.noaa.gov/regions/california-current/newport-hydrographic-line

- Pre-Recruit Survey: By request: https://www.fisheries.noaa.gov/inport/item/18603

- CalCOFI: ERDDAP, https://coastwatch.pfeg.noaa.gov/erddap/tabledap/erdCalCOFIlrvcnt.html (Dataset ID:  erdCalCOFIlrvcnt)

 Environmental data

Environmental data were extracted from a 10-km Regional Ocean Modeling System (ROMS) configured for the eastern Pacific at a 10-km resolution from 1995-2020 (Pozo Buil et al. in prep). The model was forced with daily atmospheric fields from the ERA5 reanalysis produced by European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts (Hersbach et al. 2020) and with open-ocean boundary conditions from the 1/12° Global Ocean Reanalysis and Simulation (Lellouche et al. 2021) with a five-day resolution. We extracted sea surface temperature (SST), sea surface height (SSH), sea surface salinity (SSS), and spiciness from ROMS. Spiciness was averaged over the upper 250 m of the water column, corresponding to the maximum depth sampled across the five programs. Empirical catch data collected from field sampling were matched to ROMS data using bilinear interpolation. Bottom depth (i.e., water depth at each sampling location) was extracted for each data point using R package ‘marmap’ (Pante and Simon-Bouhet 2013) which uses bathymetry 15 arc-second data from the 2022 NOAA Earth TOPOgraphy dataset (National Centers for Environmental Information [NCEI] 2022). Pacifical Decadal Oscillation values are available at https://www.ncei.noaa.gov/pub/data/cmb/ersst/v5/index/ersst.v5.pdo.dat and Oceanic Nino Index values are available at https://origin.cpc.ncep.noaa.gov/products/analysis_monitoring/ensostuff/ONI_v5.php.

 References:

stash:datasets.title: Data from: Population genomic analysis in wild medaka populations: Identifying candidate loci for balancing selection
stash:datasets.abstract: Sexual selection, defined as individual differences in reproductive success, can contribute to the maintenance of genetic polymorphisms through pleiotropic trade-offs between life history components. However, the extent to which sexual selection maintains genetic polymorphisms in wild populations remains unclear. Here, we explored genomic signatures of balancing selection and selective sweeps in the northern medaka, Oryzias sakaizumii, in Japan by performing whole-genome resequencing of wild individuals. In addition, we re-evaluated the population genetic structure and admixture of Oryzias latipes and O. sakaizumii across the Japanese archipelago and identified genomic regions largely affected by introgression between the two species using Fd statistics to distinguish signatures of balancing selection from patterns potentially caused by introgression. Based on multiple population genetic statistics, we identified 18 candidate genomic regions showing signatures of selection. In particular, a 100-kb region at 6.85-6.95 Mb on chromosome 18 showed high genetic diversity that did not show an outlier for the Fd statistics, indicating that the extent of introgression in this region did not largely differ from the genome-wide average. This pattern suggests that balancing selection maintains genetic polymorphisms of the locus in O. sakaizumii. The overlap with a QTL for female mating behavior and the known molecular function of a gene within this candidate region for balancing selection suggest that sexual selection through female mate choice may contribute to the maintenance of polymorphism at this locus.

stash:datasets.title: Genetic evaluation of reproductive strategies and breeding-site fidelity in the socially monogamous Turquoise-fronted Amazon (Amazona aestiva, Psittaciformes: Aves)

affiliations.organization: Universidad Nacional del Centro de la Provincia de Buenos Aires

stash:datasets.abstract: This dataset contains microsatellite genotype data generated and analyzed in a study of reproductive strategies and breeding-site fidelity in the socially monogamous Turquoise-fronted Amazon (Amazona aestiva). Samples were collected from wild individuals associated with monitored nesting cavities in the Federal District, Brazil, and Chaco Province, Argentina. The dataset includes multilocus genotypes obtained at six microsatellite loci, together with associated information on sample identification, nesting cavity, and sampling year. These data were used to investigate genetic relatedness and parentage within broods and to evaluate reproductive patterns, including extra-pair paternity. The dataset supports the analyses and results presented in the associated article published in the Journal of Field Ornithology.
